text: Offered him one of Folly's puppies A very smart beau Introduced to Mrs. Jennings Mrs. Jennings assured him directly that she should not stand upon ceremony Mrs. Ferrars Drawing him a little aside In a whisper "You have heard, I suppose" Talking over the business "She put in the feather last night" Listening at the door Both gained considerable amusement "Of one thing I may assure you" Showing her child to the housekeeper The gardener's lamentations Opened a window-shutter "I entreat you to stay" "I was formally dismissed" "I have entered many a shop to avoid your sight" "And see how the children go on" "I suppose you know, ma'am, that Mr. Ferrars is married" It was Edward "Everything in such respectable condition" * * * * * The family of Dashwood had long been settled in Sussex. Their estate was large, and their residence was at Norland Park, in the centre of their property, where, for many generations, they had lived in so respectable a manner as to engage the general good opinion of their surrounding acquaintance.
